thread:
Ashwin: Heads-up: I'm drafting the handoff/runbook for bringing up the new ap-southeast-4 GPU cluster. Main focus is TF->Pulumi state wiring, CI gating, and validation steps. PTAL and flag anything missing.

Maria: Thanks — do we have the backend details finalised (bucket/table/KMS)?

Ashwin: Yes. Backend plan: S3 bucket = redwood-infra-apse4-terraform, DynamoDB lock = tf-lock-apse4, KMS = arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-4:123456789012:key/redwood-apse4. Pulumi state will live in the same S3 but under pulumi/stacks/<stack>. We will enforce SSE-KMS and bucket policy to limit to the infra role.

Brian: Quotas note: AWS quota request for A10G GPUs in ap-southeast-4 already filed (case #789234). ETA ~72h. If that delays, we fallback to existing eu-gpu region via routing policy. Also cost FYI: baseline monthly reserved for 8x A10G ~ $14k/mo, spot fallback cuts by ~45%.

Maria: Can you paste the backend snippets so I can add to the module docs?

Ashwin: Sure — backend config we use in TF modules is like:

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "s3" {
    bucket = "redwood-infra-apse4-terraform"
    key    = "state/apse4/terraform.tfstate"
    region = "ap-southeast-4"
    kms_key_id = "arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-4:123456789012:key/redwood-apse4"
    dynamodb_table = "tf-lock-apse4"
  }
}
```

And Pulumi initialization steps for platform teams:

```bash
# assume infra role
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/infra-apse4-deployer --role-session-name pulumi-init

# pulumi stack init / configure backend
pulumi login s3://redwood-infra-apse4-pulumi
pulumi stack init apse4/prod
```

Ashwin: For TF->Pulumi migration we will: export TF state, map resources to Pulumi types, then use `pulumi import` for critical resources where mapping is safe. We'll keep a read-only TF state snapshot as backup: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-infra-apse4-terraform/state/apse4/terraform.tfstate tfstate-snapshot.json`.

SRE-Oncall: What are the smoke/health checks we want post-provision? Need explicit commands so oncall can validate quickly.

Ashwin: Short checklist (to include in runbook):
- `kubectl get nodes -o wide` -> all GPU nodes Ready and Kubelet version matches 1.27.x
- `kubectl get pods -n kube-system` -> core addons running
- Run tiny perf job: `kubectl run gpu-smoke -n infra --image=redwood/gpu-smoke:latest --restart=Never -- nvidia-smi`
- `curl -s http://prometheus.apse4.internal:9090/-/ready` -> metrics endpoint returns 200
- Verify KV cache integrity via small prefix test (script included)
- Run a perf trace: `./tools/run_perf.sh --region apse4 --nodes 1 --seq 512` (should complete < 45s)

Maria: CI gating: add pipeline jobs to ensure infra changes do not drift state. Proposal:
- `terraform plan` job that requires review for any changes to `aws_ssm_parameter` or `iam`
- `pulumi preview` stage that runs on PRs and fails on diffs for networking or instance types
- `integration-smoke` job that deploys to a disposable stack (apse4/canary) and runs the smoke checklist above

Ashwin: Also need to call out networking specifics:
- VPC CIDR = 10.42.0.0/16 (use /20 subnets per AZ)
- Create VPC peering to prod-backbone (route table changes + explicit allow in peer policy)
- NGW per public subnet, NATs in private zones, egress SGs locked to known egress proxies
- Ensure control-plane CIDR allowlist for SRE bastions and CI runners

Brian: FYI, inter-region replication for model artifacts: we will mirror S3 artifacts to eu-gpu for fast failover. Need replication role in apse4 bucket. Add that to IAM playbook.

SRE-Oncall: For handoff timing, we should schedule the migration window when GPU quota is confirmed and a rolling canary is allowed. Recommend Friday 03/20 03:00 UTC. I can be on-call for the window.

Ashwin: Sounds good. I'll update the runbook with explicit step-by-step and a rollback section. Rollback plan:
- If nodes fail health checks -> taint new node pools and scale down (terraform/pulumi apply revert).
- If control plane issues -> revert route table to previous backbone routes and reattach old NATs.
- Always restore TF state snapshot and Pulumi stack export from artifacts if import fails.

Maria: I added a short checklist for access + roles we need from platform-ops:
- infra-deployer role assumption (sts) allowed for CI principal
- s3:PutObject on pulumi bucket for CI service-account
- kms:Decrypt for stack secrets

devops-bot: Reminder: Please add the new bucket and DynamoDB table to infra-monitoring (alert on high read/write for locks and >50ms S3 latencies).

Brian: Also add a budget alert for the region: threshold at $25k/month initially, notify cost-team and infra-owners.

Ashwin: Great feedback. I'll push an initial runbook PR into eng-infra/runbooks and tag platform-ops + sre. Plan to run the migration 03/20 03:00 UTC if quotas clear. Will post final migration checklist here prior to run. :+1:

Maria: :+1: thanks Ashwin, will review the PR this afternoon.

SRE-Oncall: I'll stand by and watch the smoke job. Ping me 15m before start. :wave:

Ashwin: Pinged in calendar and PR created: https://git.redwood.dev/infra/runbooks/pulls/24

Brian: Approved the budget alert rule, added to cloudwatch budgets.

devops-bot: Deployment ticket created: INFRA-11244 (migration window 2026-03-20T03:00Z).
